verses.zh: 我说那承受产业的，虽然是全业的主人，但为孩童的时候却与奴仆毫无分别，
verses.en: Now I mean that the heir, as long as he is a minor,[NOTE:1] is no different from a slave, though he is the owner[NOTE:2] of everything.
notes: Grk “a small child.” The Greek term νήπιος (nēpios) refers to a young child, no longer a helpless infant but probably not more than three or four years old (L&N 9.43). The point in context, though, is that this child is too young to take any responsibility for the management of his assets.
Grk “master” or “lord” (κύριος, kurios).

verses.zh: 乃在师傅和管家的手下，直等他父亲预定的时候来到。
verses.en: But he is under guardians[NOTE:1] and managers until the date set by his[NOTE:2] father.
notes: The Greek term translated “guardians” here is ἐπίτροπος (epitropos), whose semantic domain overlaps with that of παιδαγωγός (paidagōgos) according to L&N 36.5.
Grk “the,” but the Greek article is used here as a possessive pronoun (ExSyn 215).

verses.zh: 我们为孩童的时候，受管于世俗小学之下，也是如此。
verses.en: So also we, when we were minors,[NOTE:1] were enslaved under the basic forces[NOTE:2] of the world.
notes: See the note on the word “minor” in 4:1.
Or “basic principles,” “elemental things,” or “elemental spirits.” Some interpreters take this as a reference to supernatural powers who controlled nature and/or human fate.

verses.zh: 及至时候满足，　神就差遣他的儿子，为女子所生，且生在律法以下，
verses.en: But when the appropriate time[NOTE:1] had come, God sent out his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
notes: Grk “the fullness of time” (an idiom for the totality of a period of time, with the implication of proper completion; see L&N 67.69).

verses.zh: 要把律法以下的人赎出来，叫我们得着儿子的名分。
verses.en: to redeem those who were under the law, so that we may be adopted as sons with full rights.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek term υἱοθεσία (huiothesia) was originally a legal technical term for adoption as a son with full rights of inheritance. BDAG 1024 s.v. notes, “a legal t.t. of ‘adoption’ of children, in our lit., i.e. in Paul, only in a transferred sense of a transcendent filial relationship between God and humans (with the legal aspect, not gender specificity, as major semantic component).” Although some modern translations remove the filial sense completely and render the term merely “adoption” (cf. NAB), the retention of this component of meaning was accomplished in the present translation by the phrase “as sons.”

verses.zh: 你们既为儿子，　神就差他儿子的灵进入你们（原文是我们）的心，呼叫：「阿爸！父！」
verses.en: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, who calls[NOTE:1] “Abba![NOTE:2] Father!”
notes: Grk “calling.” The participle is neuter indicating that the Spirit is the one who calls.

The term “Abba” is the Greek transliteration of the Aramaic אַבָּא (’abba’), literally meaning “my father” but taken over simply as “father,” used in prayer and in the family circle, and later taken over by the early Greek-speaking Christians (BDAG 1 s.v. ἀββα).sn This Aramaic word is found three times in the New Testament (Mark 14:36; Rom 8:15; Gal 4:6), and in each case is followed by its Greek equivalent, which is translated “father.” It is a term expressing warm affection and filial confidence. It has no perfect equivalent in English. It has passed into European languages as an ecclesiastical term, “abbot.” Over the past fifty years a lot has been written about this term and Jesus’ use of it. Joachim Jeremias argued that Jesus routinely addressed God using this Aramaic word, and he also noted this was a “child’s word,” leading many to conclude its modern equivalent was “Daddy.” This conclusion Jeremias soon modified (the term on occasion is used of an adult son addressing his father) but the simplistic equation of abba with “Daddy” is still heard in some circles today. Nevertheless, the term does express a high degree of closeness with reverence, and in addition to the family circle could be used by disciples of a much loved and revered teacher.

verses.zh: 可见，从此以后，你不是奴仆，乃是儿子了；既是儿子，就靠着　神为后嗣。
verses.en: So you are no longer a slave but a son, and if you are[NOTE:1] a son, then you are also an heir through God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “and if a son, then also an heir.” The words “you are” have been supplied twice to clarify the statement.

The unusual expression διὰ θεοῦ (dia theou, “through God”) certainly prompted scribes to alter it to more customary or theologically acceptable ones such as διὰ θεόν (dia theon, “because of God”; F G 1881), διὰ Χριστοῦ (dia Christou, “through Christ”; 81 630 sa), διὰ ᾿Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ (dia Iēsou Christou, “through Jesus Christ”; 1739c), θεοῦ διὰ Χριστοῦ (“[an heir] of God through Christ”; א2 C3 D (P) 0278 (6 326) 1175 1241 (1505) 2464 M ar sy), or κληρονόμος μὲν θεοῦ, συγκληρονόμος δὲ Χριστοῦ (klēronomos men theou, sugklēronomos de Christou, “an heir of God, and fellow-heir with Christ”; Ψ [cf. Rom 8:17]). Although it is unusual for Paul to speak of God as an intermediate agent, it is not unprecedented (cf. Gal 1:1; 1 Cor 1:9). Nevertheless, Gal 4:7 is the most direct statement to this effect. Further testimony on behalf of διὰ θεοῦ is to be found in external evidence: The witnesses with this phrase are among the most significant in the NT (P46 א* A B C* 33 1739*vid lat bo Cl).

verses.zh: 但从前你们不认识　神的时候，是给那些本来不是神的作奴仆；
verses.en: Formerly when you did not know God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods at all.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “those that by nature…” with the word “beings” implied. BDAG 1070 s.v. φύσις 2 sees this as referring to pagan worship: “Polytheists worship…beings that are by nature no gods at all Gal 4:8.”

verses.zh: 现在你们既然认识　神，更可说是被　神所认识的，怎么还要归回那懦弱无用的小学，情愿再给他作奴仆呢？
verses.en: But now that you have come to know God (or rather to be known by God), how can you turn back again to the weak and worthless[NOTE:1] basic forces?[NOTE:2] Do you want to be enslaved to them all over again?[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “useless.” See L&N 65.16.
See the note on the phrase “basic forces” in 4:3.

Grk “basic forces, to which you want to be enslaved…” Verse 9 is a single sentence in the Greek text, but has been divided into two in the translation because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence.

verses.zh: 你们谨守日子、月份、节期、年份，
verses.en: You are observing religious[NOTE:1] days and months and seasons and years.
notes: The adjective “religious” has been supplied in the translation to make clear that the problem concerns observing certain days, etc. in a religious sense (cf. NIV, NRSV “special days”). In light of the polemic in this letter against the Judaizers (those who tried to force observance of the Mosaic law on Gentile converts to Christianity) this may well be a reference to the observance of Jewish Sabbaths, feasts, and other religious days.

verses.zh: 我为你们害怕，惟恐我在你们身上是枉费了工夫。
verses.en: I fear for you that my work for you may have been in vain.

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我劝你们要像我一样，因为我也像你们一样。你们一点没有亏负我。
verses.en: I beg you, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] become like me, because I have become like you. You have done me no wrong!
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:11.

verses.zh: 你们知道我头一次传福音给你们，是因为身体有疾病。
verses.en: But you know it was because of a physical illness that I first proclaimed the gospel to you,

verses.zh: 你们为我身体的缘故受试炼，没有轻看我，也没有厌弃我，反倒接待我，如同　神的使者，如同基督耶稣。
verses.en: and though my physical condition put you to the test, you did not despise or reject me.[NOTE:1] Instead, you welcomed me as though I were an angel of God,[NOTE:2] as though I were Christ Jesus himself![NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “your trial in my flesh you did not despise or reject.”

Or “the angel of God.” Linguistically, “angel of God” is the same in both testaments (and thus, he is either “an angel of God” or “the angel of God” in both testaments). For arguments and implications, see ExSyn 252; M. J. Davidson, “Angels,” DJG, 9; W. G. MacDonald argues for “an angel” in both testaments: “Christology and ‘The Angel of the Lord’,” Current Issues in Biblical and Patristic Interpretation, 324-35.

Grk “as an angel of God…as Christ Jesus.” This could be understood to mean either “you welcomed me like an angel of God would,” or “you welcomed me as though I were an angel of God.” In context only the second is accurate, so the translation has been phrased to indicate this.

verses.zh: 你们当日所夸的福气在哪里呢？那时你们若能行，就是把自己的眼睛剜出来给我，也都情愿。这是我可以给你们作见证的。
verses.en: Where then is your sense of happiness[NOTE:1] now? For I testify about you that if it were possible, you would have pulled out your eyes and given them to me!
notes: Or “blessedness.”

verses.zh: 如今我将真理告诉你们，就成了你们的仇敌吗？
verses.en: So then, have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “have I become your enemy because I am telling you the truth?” The participle ἀληθεύων (alētheuōn) can be translated as a causal adverbial participle or as a participle of means (as in the translation).

verses.zh: 那些人热心待你们，却不是好意，是要离间你们（原文是把你们关在外面），叫你们热心待他们。
verses.en: They court you eagerly,[NOTE:1] but for no good purpose;[NOTE:2] they want to exclude you, so that you would seek them eagerly.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “They are zealous for you.”
Or “but not commendably” (BDAG 505 s.v. καλῶς 2).
Or “so that you would be zealous.”

verses.zh: 在善事上，常用热心待人原是好的，却不单我与你们同在的时候才这样。
verses.en: However, it is good[NOTE:1] to be sought eagerly[NOTE:2] for a good purpose[NOTE:3] at all times, and not only when I am present with you.
notes: Or “commendable.”
Or “to be zealous.”
Grk “But it is always good to be zealous in good.”

verses.zh: 我小子啊，我为你们再受生产之苦，直等到基督成形在你们心里。
verses.en: My children—I am again undergoing birth pains until Christ is formed in you![NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “My children, for whom I am again undergoing birth pains until Christ is formed in you.” The relative clauses in English do not pick up the emotional force of Paul’s language here (note “tone of voice” in v. 20, indicating that he is passionately concerned for them); hence, the translation has been altered slightly to capture the connotative power of Paul’s plea.sn That is, until Christ’s nature or character is formed in them (see L&N 58.4).

verses.zh: 我巴不得现今在你们那里，改换口气，因我为你们心里作难。
verses.en: I wish I could be with you now and change my tone of voice,[NOTE:1] because I am perplexed about you.
notes: Grk “voice” or “tone.” The contemporary English expression “tone of voice” is a good approximation to the meaning here.

verses.zh: 你们这愿意在律法以下的人，请告诉我，你们岂没有听见律法吗？
verses.en: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand the law?[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “will you not hear what the law says?” The Greek verb ἀκούω (akouō) means “hear, listen to,” but by figurative extension it can also mean “obey.” It can also refer to the process of comprehension that follows hearing, and that sense fits the context well here.

verses.zh: 因为律法上记着，亚伯拉罕有两个儿子，一个是使女生的，一个是自主之妇人生的。
verses.en: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the[NOTE:1] slave woman and the other by the free woman.
notes: Paul’s use of the Greek article here and before the phrase “free woman” presumes that both these characters are well known to the recipients of his letter. This verse is given as an example of the category called “well-known (‘celebrity’ or ‘familiar’) article” by ExSyn 225.

verses.zh: 然而，那使女所生的是按着血气生的；那自主之妇人所生的是凭着应许生的。
verses.en: But one, the son by the slave woman, was born by natural descent,[NOTE:1] while the other, the son by the free woman, was born through the promise.
notes: Grk “born according to the flesh”; BDAG 916 s.v. σάρξ 4 has “Of natural descent τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκός children by natural descent Ro 9:8 (opp. τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας). ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται Gal 4:23; cp. vs. 29.”

verses.zh: 这都是比方：那两个妇人就是两约。一约是出于西奈山，生子为奴，乃是夏甲。
verses.en: These things may be treated as an allegory,[NOTE:1] for these women represent two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai bearing children for slavery; this is Hagar.
notes: Grk “which things are spoken about allegorically.” Paul is not saying the OT account is an allegory, but rather that he is constructing an allegory based on the OT account.

verses.zh: 这夏甲二字是指着阿拉伯的西奈山，与现在的耶路撒冷同类，因耶路撒冷和她的儿女都是为奴的。
verses.en: Now Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.

verses.zh: 但那在上的耶路撒冷是自主的，她是我们的母。
verses.en: But the Jerusalem above is free,[NOTE:1] and she is our mother.
notes: The meaning of the statement the Jerusalem above is free is that the other woman represents the second covenant (cf. v. 24); she corresponds to the Jerusalem above that is free. Paul’s argument is very condensed at this point.

verses.zh: 因为经上记着：不怀孕、不生养的，你要欢乐；未曾经过产难的，你要高声欢呼；因为没有丈夫的，比有丈夫的儿女更多。
verses.en: For it is written:“Rejoice, O barren woman who does not bear children;[NOTE:1] break forth and shout, you who have no birth pains,because the children of the desolate woman are more numerousthan those of the woman who has a husband.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The direct object “children” is not in the Greek text, but has been supplied for clarity. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
Grk “because more are the children of the barren one than of the one having a husband.”sn A quotation from Isa 54:1.

verses.zh: 弟兄们，我们是凭着应许作儿女，如同以撒一样。
verses.en: But you,[NOTE:1] brothers and sisters,[NOTE:2] are children of the promise like Isaac.
notes: Most mss (א A C D2 Ψ 062 1241 1505 2464 M lat sy bo) read “we” here, while “you” is found in P46 B D* F G 0261vid 0278 33 1175 1739 al sa. It is more likely that a copyist, noticing the first person pronouns in vv. 26 and 31, changed a second person pronoun here to first person for consistency.
Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:11.

verses.zh: 当时，那按着血气生的逼迫了那按着圣灵生的，现在也是这样。
verses.en: But just as at that time the one born by natural descent[NOTE:1] persecuted the one born according to the Spirit,[NOTE:2] so it is now.
notes: Grk “according to the flesh”; see the note on the phrase “by natural descent” in 4:23.
Or “the one born by the Spirit’s [power].”

verses.zh: 然而经上是怎么说的呢？是说：「把使女和她儿子赶出去！因为使女的儿子不可与自主妇人的儿子一同承受产业。」
verses.en: But what does the scripture say? “Throw out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will not share the inheritance with the son”[NOTE:1] of the free woman.
notes: A quotation from Gen 21:10. The phrase of the free woman does not occur in Gen 21:10.

verses.zh: 弟兄们，这样看来，我们不是使女的儿女，乃是自主妇人的儿女了。
verses.en: Therefore, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:11.
